source: Independently composed constructive maximum matching, Tutte-Berge and Gallai-Edmonds task.
worker_visibility: Never mount or copy this directory into worker containers.
expected_answer: Self-contained polynomial blossom algorithm, a tight Tutte-Berge witness, and a proved and constructible Gallai-Edmonds decomposition for every finite simple graph.
criteria: Precise deterministic algorithm returning a maximum matching; search, state, contraction and lifting are sufficiently specified to execute.
Derives augmenting-path criterion and all needed blossom/contraction/lifting statements with exact hypotheses. Nested contractions preserve a valid matching and original endpoint information.
Proves progress and termination; does not conflate a larger lifted matching with a maximum matching in the original graph.
Proves 2|N| <= n+|U|-o(G-U) for all matchings N and U, and computes a U attaining equality for the returned M in polynomial time.
Defines D by vertices exposable by some maximum matching, A=N(D) minus D, and C as complement; proves factor-criticality of every D component and existence of a perfect matching on C.

Proves the claimed structure for EVERY maximum matching: perfect on C, internally near-perfect on each D component, and all A vertices matched into distinct D components. Also proves the converse and tightness of U=A.
Computes D,A,C in polynomial time. Repeated maximum-matching calls are allowed if justified and included in the bound.
Explicit polynomial word-operation bounds under stated representations cover all subroutines including nested contraction, original endpoint records, certificate and decomposition.
Handles empty/disconnected graphs, isolated vertices, perfect matching case, and singleton factor-critical components.
Every matching theorem used is proved. Standard elementary arguments and graph traversal are permitted. No exponential subset enumeration disguised as a polynomial step.
common_failure_modes: Unjustified assertion that an arbitrary odd cycle can be contracted for matching optimization.
Assumes a maximum matching of a contracted graph always lifts to a maximum matching of the original graph; requires additional conditions or iterative augmentation.
Confuses alternating walks with simple alternating/augmenting paths, or reachable parity before and after contractions without proof.
Leaves nested blossom expansion undefined or loses original endpoints when identifying parallel edges.
Claims factor-criticality or Gallai-Edmonds structure from an unproved matching theorem, or proves the structure for only one maximum matching.
Uses an unproved Hall or Tutte theorem, or constructs certificate/decomposition by exponential enumeration.
Counts only augmentations while allowing exponential recursive work within an augmentation.
Submits a plausible algorithm sketch with major proof obligations deferred.
review_policy: Review the full submission against every obligation; AI review is not formal verification. The reference is a guide, not permission to assume omitted arguments or copy errors. Accept any valid fully proved implementation of the requested blossom-based approach. Record unresolved gaps as uncertain or incorrect. Calibration qualification depends on correctness and measured single-agent latency only.
